title: LdInterfaces
description: Generated by tools/bundle.py from schemas/. Do not edit.

BufferTemplate.description: Storage template. Every buffer instance has exactly one bidirectional MATERIAL port, named io and addressed as <buffer_id>.io in connections (LD-PEC-002 §3, Q-08).

CatalogBundle.description: Transport form of a whole catalog: the manifest plus every entry inline. Used by I-1 create and restore.

CatalogManifest.description: Binds a catalog. Its own hash, in domain ld.catalog.v0, is the catalog_hash.

ClaimView.description: Read-only view derived solely from state (LD-PEC-002 §5.4).

lots.description: Every lot on the claim: inventory (products, kits, raw material) and buffer contents. Lots inside a buffer also appear in its BufferView totals.

deposits.description: Deposits on the claim, with what remains and what has been extracted. Each has a face port, <deposit_id>.face, that a FEED can draw from (LD-PEC-005 §3.3).

sinks.description: Material and heat sinks: cumulative losses, tailings and waste heat.

ConnectionTemplate.description: How a connection behaves (LD-PEC-002 §3). FEED couples a machine material port to a buffer's io port; the transfer is part of the machine's own operation, so it has no transit delay. CONVEYOR links two buffers; material moves only as TRANSFER_LOCAL shipments, which take time at the throughput and then the transit delay.

reservations.description: STOCK held for running jobs that feed from this deposit's face port (LD-PEC-005 §3.3). Omitted when empty.

EnergyStoreInstance.description: An installed energy store; store_id is its machine. Charge and capacity are in the bus energy unit; the fraction of charge is the residual (store_id, charge).

EnergyView.description: Bus power in the unit given, per microsecond.

segments.description: Piecewise-constant values; start_us ascending, first is "0".

Event.description: Append-only event log entry, tagged by "kind".

ExpectedHashes.description: expected/hashes.json: state hash and history head after each script step, by step index.

table.description: Required for lookup: piecewise-linear breakpoints over an integer domain.

environment.description: Environment function ids active on this claim.

HistoryRecord.description: Hashed in domain ld.pec.history.v1 (LD-PEC-001 §9.1, LD-PEC-004 §8). The history root is H(ld.pec.history.v1, {genesis_hash, world, claim}).

Id.description: Stable identifier, unique within its scope. A job id may be reused once the job has left the physical state (LD-PEC-004 A2-1); other ids are never reused.

Instruction.description: One primitive of pset_version 0 (LD-PEC-003 §10), tagged by "op". DISASSEMBLE and SELECT arrive in a later pset_version.

vector.description: Species to signed integer coefficient; negative consumes, positive produces.

draw.description: Material this PARTITION draws itself, per unit of extent, from the input port named by `input`: species to a whole-multiple extent expression. Lets a stage that only splits material, such as a screen, say how much one unit is (LD-PEC-005 §3.8). Absent: `input` names the stage's pool or a stream.

components.description: Component product id to count per unit produced.

part_load.description: PER_WORK DRAW only: power against load while the job runs (LD-PEC-004 A3-4). Points of (load, power) as fractions: load is the job's rate over its blueprint's rated_work, power the draw over this op's draw at rated_work. Linear between points and extended beyond the first and last. Loads strictly increase within [0, 1]; power never decreases and is never below load. The difference from the plain per-work draw is heat at once, in the process's heat sink (LD-PEC-004 A3-4). Without it, power is proportional to load.

Int.description: Signed integer as a canonical decimal string. No "-0", no leading zeros, no "+".

IssuedBy.description: Which application issued a command (LD-PEC-004 A5, LD-PEC-009 §7). Recorded with the command in its history record, so the hash chain commits to it; it plays no part in physics. The claim host fills it: origin from the browser-verified origin of the sending page, or "host" for the host's own interface. app_name is the application's own description of itself.

started.description: True once START is admitted. Only started jobs are dispatched.

products.description: Discrete products in this lot: product id to count.

idle_power.description: Power drawn while installed and not running, in the power unit named by unit (per second, as W). Served after jobs; unmet idle draw only marks the machine unpowered (LD-PEC-005 §8.3).

core.description: Material the machine carries inside it, such as a reactor's fuel (LD-PEC-004 A2-3). INSTALL also installs a buffer of the given template as <machine>-core, linked to each listed port by a connection of the given template (<machine>-core-<port>): from the core for an input port, to it for an output. The core and its links cannot be connected, disconnected or removed on their own; REMOVE of the machine puts the core's contents in the kit lot.

ports.description: Material ports of this blueprint linked to the core.

energy_store.description: Makes the machine an energy store on the claim bus, such as a battery (LD-PEC-005 §8.2).

unpowered.description: Present and true when the machine's idle draw is not being met (LD-PEC-005 §8.3).

NextEventTime.description: t_us is absent when no event is scheduled.

PhysicalState.description: Canonical state; hashed in domain ld.pec.physical-state.v1. Every array is sorted by its first id field.

environment.description: Environment functions in effect on this claim, copied from genesis; sorted.

PortRef.description: A port or stage endpoint inside a process: "port:<id>", "stage:<id>" (the stage's pool), or "stage:<id>.<stream>" (a named stream the stage makes, LD-PEC-005 §3.2).

PositiveInt.description: Positive integer as a canonical decimal string.

dispatch.description: For a process that produces power: MUST_RUN (the default) runs as fast as it can and surplus is curtailed; FOLLOW_LOAD runs only as fast as the bus needs, after stores (LD-PEC-006 §3.2.2).

restart_thresholds.description: Level switches per port (LD-PEC-004 A4). An input's level is its buffer's available stock of the port's species; an output's is its buffer's headroom (free space). A stopped job restarts only once the level reaches the restart level; a running FLOW job stops when it would take the level past the stop level. Give levels either as amounts (restart_at, stop_at, in unit) or as fractions of the connected buffer's capacity (restart_fraction, stop_fraction), not both. The stop level is below the restart level.

Quantity.description: An amount in a catalog-declared unit.

Rational.description: Exact rational. Must be reduced; zero is {n: "0", d: "1"}. Reduction is a semantic check, not a schema check.

Reason.description: Deterministic explanation of a job's status, tagged by "code": why a started job is not running, or how a running one is limited (DWELLING, FED, FEED_UNSETTLED).

Reservation.description: Quantity of a buffer held for one holder, a job or a shipment. STOCK holds material in the buffer for the holder to draw; SPACE holds free capacity for material the holder will deliver.

Response.description: Any I-1 response, tagged by "method"; failures use method "error".

ScriptStep.description: One line of script.jsonl, tagged by "step".

SpeciesAmounts.description: Map from substance id to quantity in that substance's catalog unit.

formula.description: Element id to atom count per formula unit.

latent_to.description: Target phase species to energy per quantity unit, in joules.

TimeUs.description: Signed 64-bit microseconds since world genesis, as a decimal string.

Uint.description: Unsigned integer as a canonical decimal string: "0" or a nonzero digit followed by digits.

VectorManifest.description: vector.json at the root of each vector directory.

id.description: Spec vector id, e.g. V-05 (LD-PEC-001 §11) or P-01 (LD-PEC-003 §11), with an optional letter suffix.

kind.description: EXECUTION vectors replay commands; ADMISSION vectors check a catalog against LD-PEC-003 §8.

status.description: DRAFT until expected outputs are produced by one implementation and confirmed by the other.
